main_text.head: Materiae in prima notione consideratae competit,
Habere actum, qui omni Enti extra causas constituto communis est.
main_text.p: I. Duplex à Scoto actus constituitur, formalis & Entitativus. Formalis est per quem substantia completa corporea ad certam aliquam speciem completam & perfectam restricta est.
Entitativus est Entis extra causas suas constitutio, seu existentia: Quod enim adhuc in causis est, vocatur Ens potentia: quod extra causas est, vocatur Ens actu.

II. De actu formali nulla est controversia. Fatentur enim omnes, materiam primam in se ut Ens consideratam carere forma, quod theseos huius decimae membro primo demonstravimus. Sed de actu Entitativo acerrime contendunt philosophi. Affirmantem tuentur Scotus, Gregorius Arminensis, Mercenarius, Pererius, & Philippus Faber Scoti defensor: Negantem vero pleriq; alij Peripatetici, inprimis Thomas & ejus assecla: Inter recentiores magno conatu rem hanc agit Zabarella.

III. Sensus igitur quaestionis: An materia prima habeat actum Entitativum: Ex mente Philippi Fabri, qui Scoti sententias quàm diligentissimè explanat, Philosophiae naturalis theoremate 22. cap.1. hic est: An materia prima habeat entitatem positivam, & extra suas causas constitutam ? Vel: An mate-

page.notes: The right-hand facing page is cut off at the scan edge. Its text lines and any marginal notes are illegible, so they are marked as such and not read. The gutter-side strip shows partial Greek or Latin text, but no reliable reading is possible. The left page is read fully. The catchword "ria" is taken from the bottom right of the left page. The printed text ends with "mate-", a hyphen at the line end, and continues in the next page. Greek word "Ἐξήγησις" is copied as printed, with its accents as far as they are visible. No printing errors were judged with confidence.
